summary: Uetze (about 22,000 residents, with Dedenhausen, Dollbergen, Haenigsen and Eltze among its villages) has no municipal parking tariff, parking-disc zone or Stellplatz statute that the researcher could find (absence is not proven), and the parking material visible in public sources is mostly about the two rail park-and-ride sites, which belong to the Region Hannover's system and are shown as free of charge on the Region's portal. The Region Hannover's Nahverkehrsplan 2021 (cover dated April 2022) rates Dollbergen priority 1 (high) and Dedenhausen priority 2 (medium) for park-and-ride, and says park-and-ride and bike-and-ride use is currently free but may be charged in future. Before the extension, up to 150 rail customers' cars were counted daily around Dollbergen's overloaded lots, and in September 2021 local press reported 133 additional spaces open on top of the 84 previously available, with a 160-place bike facility to follow; the portal now shows 133 spaces in total, which no source reconciles. The Region's portal lists Dedenhausen with 62 spaces (its figures do not add up and its data record says 114), DB lists 50 there and 40+44+28 at Dollbergen, and a 2020 party statement relayed a Region answer that nearly all of 113 Dedenhausen spaces were occupied on weekdays. The municipality announced ground-sensor work for a digital parking guidance system at Dedenhausen for March 2023 (completion not reported) and reported more than 100 new bike spaces there in June 2024; on 21 October 2026 it reported that the Dollbergen bike cage is being kept open because its electronic lock keeps failing. In the centre, the municipality received its first fast-charging station (2 x 50 kW) at the town hall in July 2023, announced its first parklet for 26 September 2023, and ran a Hindenburgplatz traffic trial between June and August 2024; the January 2025 evaluation slides found no clear drop in traffic volumes but lower speeds, and an on-site survey of 297 people found 47 and 43 percent had arrived by own car, with 93 percent of those finding a space directly. A University household survey in 2024 found 56.9 percent use a car or motorbike daily or almost daily. A DB corridor renovation between Hannover and Berlin runs from October 2026 to December 2027, but the DB release does not name the two Uetze stations.

items.text: DB's station parking pages (read 21 October 2026) list one open lot with 50 spaces at Dedenhausen (Zum Bahnhof) and three open lots at Dollbergen (Ladestraße 40, Bahnhofstraße 81 44, Berliner Allee 2 28), all open around the clock; these DB figures differ from the Region Hannover's own counts.
items.source_title: Bahnhof Dollbergen and Bahnhof Dedenhausen - Parken (bahnhof.de)

items.text: The Region Hannover portal run by VMZ Niedersachsen (read 21 October 2026) lists P+R Dollbergen (Ackerbergstraße) with 133 car spaces plus 2 for reduced mobility, free of charge, 160 roofed bike places and 10 motorcycle places. It shows live free-space counts and hourly average profiles, and RE 30 to Hannover Hbf runs hourly around midday, plus buses 946 and 950 and on-demand AST service.
items.source_title: Region Hannover Park + Ride: Dollbergen (VMZ Niedersachsen)

items.text: The same portal (read 21 October 2026) lists P+R Dedenhausen (near B444, Zum Bahnhof) with a headline of 62 spaces, free of charge, in two areas (Nord: 9 car spaces plus 2 for reduced mobility; Sued: 51 car spaces plus 2 for reduced mobility, which sums to 64 rather than 62), 58 bike places and lockable bike garages. RE 30 and bus 950 serve the stop, and the page carries live and hourly utilisation displays. The page's underlying data record lists 114 car spaces, so the 62 shown may cover only part of the site.
items.source_title: Region Hannover Park + Ride: Dedenhausen (Nähe B444) (VMZ Niedersachsen)

items.text: The Region Hannover's Nahverkehrsplan 2021 (cover dated April 2022) says the Region is the responsible authority and often the builder of park-and-ride sites, financed with state and federal funds, while the municipalities or the infra company own, administer and maintain them. It says use of bike+ride and park+ride sites is currently free of charge, that this may change in future, and that fees could make sense for casual users of bike garages or for users of parking decks.

The Nahverkehrsplan 2021 aims to provide P+R at all rail stations close to where people live. In its station priority table (updated in 2018 from utilisation counts) Dollbergen is priority 1 (high) for P+R and bike+ride, and Dedenhausen priority 2 (medium) for P+R and 3 for bike+ride.

In its description of bike+ride garages, the Nahverkehrsplan 2021 (cover dated April 2022) says that, according to experience so far, charging options are not strongly demanded by daily commuters and that e-charging options are not demanded. The passage is in the bike+ride section and does not say whether it concerns e-bike or car charging.

On 23 October 2019 the Region Hannover's transport committee approved about 1.1 million euros in pre-financing for a Dollbergen station redesign; up to 150 rail customers' cars were counted daily around the full car parks, there were 57 spaces south and 27 north, about 1,700 people used the station on weekdays, and 133 more spaces (a possible 92 beyond that) were planned.
items.source_title: Bahnhof Dollbergen: Mehr Platz und Komfort für Pendler (AltkreisBlitz)

items.text: On 28 September 2021 AltkreisBlitz reported that the new Dollbergen P+R area with 133 additional car spaces was open for use (planting and signage still to come, lighting working), on top of the 84 spaces previously available on the north and south sides. A step-free bus stop, a new bike+ride facility for 160 bicycles replacing the existing one, and ten motorcycle spaces were to follow; the Region expected total costs of about 1.1 million euros.
items.source_title: Neuer Park-and-ride-Platz in Uetze-Dollbergen ist ab sofort nutzbar (AltkreisBlitz)

items.text: The municipality announced that the northern part of the Dedenhausen P+R lot would be closed on 9-10 March 2023 so a contractor (SO NAH, Aachen) could install ground sensors for a digital parking guidance system.
items.source_title: Vollsperrung des P + R Parkplatzes Dedenhausen (Gemeinde Uetze, Pressedienst Nr. 16)

items.text: In June 2024 the municipality reported more than 100 new bicycle spaces at Dedenhausen station, funded under DB's Bike+Ride programme, used by commuters towards Hannover or Wolfsburg and well taken up soon after completion.
items.source_title: Neue Fahrradabstellmöglichkeiten am Bahnhof in Dedenhausen errichtet (Gemeinde Uetze)

items.text: On 21 October 2026 the municipality reported that the electronic locking system of the Dollbergen bike+ride cage has repeatedly failed, so the Region Hannover, as operator, keeps the cage open until the fault is fixed.

In July 2023 BayWa r.e. handed over Uetze's first fast-charging station (2 x 50 kW) at the town hall in Marktstraße near the B188, run by Ladegrün for the municipal company and advertised at 50 cents per kWh.
items.source_title: BayWa r.e. übergibt offiziell E-Ladesäule an Gemeindebetrieb Uetze (press release 5 July 2023)

items.text: A municipal notice of 21 September 2023 (updated 25 September) announced that the first Uetze parklet, a wooden (larch) seating structure of the kind that stands on parking areas instead of parked cars and was provided free of charge by the Mobilnetzwerk Hannover and the Region Hannover, would be officially handed over and opened on Tuesday 26 September 2023 at 13:00 at Apothekenstrasse 1. The page does not report the event itself.
items.source_title: Ein Parklet fuer Uetze - Parklet statt Parkplatz (Gemeinde Uetze), announcement

items.text: From June 2024 Uetze trialled speed 20 on Kaiserstraße and one-way traffic on Bentestraße around Hindenburgplatz, later with part of Bentestraße closed. The January 2025 evaluation found no clear fall in traffic volumes but lower speeds, about 70 percent support for speed 20, and in the on-site survey 47 and 43 percent arrived by own car (two stages) with 93 percent of car arrivals finding a space directly.

A University of Hannover household survey (May-June 2024, about 2,000 returns from Ortsteil Uetze) found 56.9 percent use a car or motorbike daily or almost daily; the authors conclude car traffic is very important locally because public transport is weak or seen as weak.
items.source_title: Verkehr in der Ortschaft Uetze: Haushaltsbefragung 2024 (Leibniz Universität Hannover)

items.text: The municipality's retail concept update (CIMA, 2019, adopted by the council) names the Uetze centre around Hindenburgplatz as main centre and suggests linking the Edeka customer car park with Hindenburgplatz to improve walking access; it sets no parking tariffs or zones.
items.source_title: Fortschreibung des Einzelhandelskonzeptes für die Gemeinde Uetze 2019

items.text: DB InfraGO announced (9 September 2026; posted by the municipality 9 October 2026) a Hannover-Berlin corridor renovation from 2 October 2026 to December 2027, with the Lehrter Stammbahn largely closed to trains and a detailed regional rail concept from December 2026 still being agreed, with replacement buses planned. The release does not name Dollbergen or Dedenhausen.
items.source_title: Presseinformation Deutsche Bahn Bau- und Verkehrskonzept (via Gemeinde Uetze)

gaps: No municipal parking tariff, parking-disc zone, resident-parking or Stellplatzsatzung found: the uetze.de search for these terms returned none, and the Ortsrecht index (PDF dated January 2013) lists no parking statute; absence is not proven and the current Ortsrecht pages were not fully opened.
Uetze council information system (uetze.de Ratsinformationssystem, allris paths returned 404) and Region Hannover committee papers on Dedenhausen P+R expansion could not be opened or found.

https://www.deutscherpresseindex.de/?p=688886 (copy of the Region press release on the Dollbergen opening) showed only a maintenance page; the AltkreisBlitz report was used instead. The original Region Hannover press release was not found.
https://www.mw.niedersachsen.de/download/114252/OePNV_Flaechenprogramm.pdf returned a maintenance page (state funding list).
Bebauungsplan Nr. 7 'Zum Bahnhof' Dedenhausen (uetze.de PDFs BP_02_07 and BP_02_07A) are scanned images without readable text, so any link to a P+R extension could not be checked.

Why the Region portal shows 62 Dedenhausen and 133 Dollbergen spaces while DB lists 50 and 40+44+28, and whether the Dollbergen 133 is the total or the 2021 addition, is not explained by any source read; the 2021 reports say 133 were added to 84 existing spaces.

No source found on the Dedenhausen P+R construction date, any enlargement after 2020, EV charging at the stations, or utilisation statements beyond the 2019 and 2020 reports; Uetze's bus lines (946, 950, AST/sprinti) were seen only as names on the VMZ portal.

Verkehrsversuch decisions by the council after January 2025 (whether Kaiserstraße speed 20 or Bentestraße changes became permanent) were not found; trial figures come from presentation slides and a survey chart mapping for parking-related questions was too ambiguous to use.
The Region's night parking ban (since May 2025) applies to 20 Stadtbahn P+R sites per the Region's page and was not recorded as applying to Uetze's rail sites.
